faqs.a: No. Merge PDF runs entirely in your browser using pdf-lib — your files never leave your device.

faqs.q: Is there a limit on how many PDFs I can merge?

faqs.q: Can I reorder pages before merging?
faqs.a: Yes, drag files into the order you want before combining them into the final PDF.

points.title: Reports built from separate sections
points.desc: When a report is drafted in pieces — cover page, chapters, appendix — merging is how those pieces become the single document you actually submit.

points.title: Scanned pages that arrived as separate files
points.desc: A scanner or phone scanning app often saves each page as its own PDF. Merge PDF turns that pile back into one ordered document.

tools.name: Protect PDF
tools.title: Password Protect PDF Free Online | YOYOPDF
tools.description: Add a password to a PDF to restrict opening or editing. Free, browser-based encryption — see the tool for encryption details.
tools.shortDesc: Add an open or permissions password to a PDF file.

faqs.q: How strong is the encryption?
faqs.a: Protect PDF uses the PDF format's original Standard Security Handler (40-bit RC4). It's suitable as basic access control, not as strong confidentiality for highly sensitive documents.

faqs.q: Is my file uploaded to encrypt it?
faqs.a: No, encryption happens locally in your browser — the file and password are never sent anywhere.

faqs.q: Can I restrict printing or editing without a password to open?
faqs.a: Yes, permission flags can be set independently of the open password, though they're honored only by readers that respect them.

whyUse.intro: A password on a PDF is a simple gate against casual access — the file only opens for someone who has the password you gave them, not for anyone who happens to receive the attachment.

points.title: A file is going somewhere less controlled than a private inbox
points.desc: Cloud storage links, shared drives, and forwarded emails all widen who might end up with a copy — a password limits who can actually open it.

points.title: Printing or editing needs to stay restricted
points.desc: Permission flags can lock down printing or editing even for readers who have the open password, in readers that respect those flags.

points.title: Basic access control is the actual requirement
points.desc: For everyday documents that just need a gate — not vault-grade confidentiality — a standard PDF password is a fast, no-install way to add one.
